title: GATE CS Topic Test — Digital Logic (Set 1)
titleEn: GATE CS Topic Test — Digital Logic (Set 1)

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about decoders and multiplexers are TRUE?
optionsEn: A 3-to-8 decoder has 8 select lines and 3 outputs
Any Boolean function of n variables can be implemented using a 2^(n-1)-to-1 MUX and at most one inverter
A demultiplexer with its data input tied to logic 1 functions as a decoder
An n-to-2^n active-high decoder generates all 2^n minterms of its n input variables
questions.explanationEn: An n-to-2^n decoder outputs all minterms, a 2^(n-1)-to-1 MUX can realize any n-variable function using Shannon expansion, and a 1-to-2^n DEMUX with data=1 acts as an n-to-2^n decoder. A 3-to-8 decoder has 3 inputs and 8 outputs, making C false.

questions.questionTextEn: Which flip-flop eliminates the invalid/forbidden input state present in an SR flip-flop by toggling its output when both inputs are 1?
questions.explanationEn: A JK flip-flop behaves like an SR flip-flop for (0,0), (0,1), and (1,0), and toggles Q -> Q' when J = 1 and K = 1, removing the indeterminate state.

questions.questionTextEn: In IEEE 754 single-precision (32-bit) floating-point format, what is the exponent bias and how many bits are allocated to the mantissa (fraction) field?
questions.explanationEn: IEEE 754 binary32 uses 1 sign bit, 8 exponent bits (bias = 2^7 - 1 = 127), and 23 explicit fraction/mantissa bits (with 1 implicit leading bit for normalized numbers).

questions.questionTextEn: A half-adder can be implemented using:
optionsEn: One XOR gate and one AND gate
One XOR gate and one OR gate
Two AND gates and one OR gate
One XNOR gate and one NAND gate
questions.explanationEn: For inputs A and B, a half-adder produces Sum = A ⊕ B (XOR) and Carry = A · B (AND).

questions.questionTextEn: Consider addition of two n-bit signed integers in 2's complement representation. Which of the following statements are ALWAYS TRUE?
optionsEn: Overflow can never occur when adding two numbers of opposite signs
Overflow occurs if and only if the carry into the MSB differs from the carry out of the MSB
A carry out of the MSB always indicates signed overflow
Negating the most negative n-bit number (-2^(n-1)) causes overflow
questions.explanationEn: Adding opposite-signed numbers stays within bounds (A is true). Signed overflow is detected by Cin_MSB ⊕ Cout_MSB = 1 (B is true). Negating -2^(n-1) gives +2^(n-1), which exceeds 2^(n-1)-1 (D is true). Carry-out alone indicates unsigned overflow, not signed overflow (C is false).

questions.questionTextEn: What is the decimal value of the 8-bit 2's complement signed binary number 11101011?
questions.explanationEn: Since the MSB is 1, the number is negative. Taking the 2's complement: invert bits to 00010100 (20) and add 1 to get 00010101 (21). Hence the signed value is -21.

questions.questionTextEn: What is the minimum number of 2-to-1 multiplexers required to construct a 16-to-1 multiplexer?
questions.explanationEn: Building an N-to-1 MUX tree from 2-to-1 MUXes requires N - 1 units: 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 15.

questions.questionTextEn: What is the minimum number of 2-to-4 decoders (with enable input) required to construct a 4-to-16 decoder?
questions.explanationEn: Four 2-to-4 decoders generate the 16 outputs (controlled by the lower 2 bits), and one 2-to-4 decoder decodes the upper 2 bits to drive their enable lines, totaling 4 + 1 = 5 decoders.

questions.questionTextEn: What is the hexadecimal equivalent of the octal number (357)_8?
questions.explanationEn: Convert (357)_8 to binary: 011 101 111 = 011101111. Group in 4 bits from right: 1110 1111 = (EF)_16.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following are valid differences between synchronous and asynchronous (ripple) counters?
optionsEn: All flip-flops in a synchronous counter share the same clock signal
Ripple counters suffer from cumulative propagation delay across stages
Synchronous counters generally support higher maximum clock frequencies than ripple counters of the same bit-width
Ripple counters always require more flip-flops than synchronous counters for the same modulus
questions.explanationEn: Synchronous counters clock all flip-flops simultaneously, avoiding ripple delay and enabling higher clock speeds. Both counter types use the same minimum number of flip-flops ceil(log2(M)) for modulus M, so D is false.

questions.questionTextEn: A 4-bit ripple counter counts from 0000 to 1111 continuously. An AND gate with inputs Q3 and Q1 (MSB is Q3) is connected to the asynchronous active-high CLEAR input of all flip-flops. What is the modulus (number of stable states) of this counter?
questions.explanationEn: Q3 and Q1 are both 1 for the first time at binary 1010 (decimal 10), which immediately clears the counter to 0000. Thus the counter cycles through stable states 0 to 9 (modulus = 10, a decade counter).

questions.questionTextEn: A 3-bit Linear Feedback Shift Register (LFSR) with state (Q2, Q1, Q0) updates according to Q2_next = Q1 ⊕ Q0, Q1_next = Q2, Q0_next = Q1. Starting from (1, 0, 0), after how many clock pulses does the state (1, 0, 0) repeat for the first time?
questions.explanationEn: Trace: 100 -> 010 -> 101 -> 110 -> 111 -> 011 -> 001 -> 100. This primitive polynomial x^3 + x + 1 generates a maximal-length sequence of 2^3 - 1 = 7 states.

questions.questionTextEn: To convert a D flip-flop into a JK flip-flop, what Boolean expression must be connected to the D input?
questions.explanationEn: The next state of a JK flip-flop is Q(t+1) = J·Q' + K'·Q. Since a D flip-flop satisfies Q(t+1) = D, setting D = J·Q' + K'·Q directly realizes JK behavior.

questions.questionTextEn: A Moore machine has 5 states (S0, S1, S2, S3, S4) over binary input {0, 1}. S0 and S2 both output 0 and transition on 0 to S1, on 1 to S3. S1 and S4 both output 1 and transition on 0 to S0, on 1 to S2. S3 outputs 0 and transitions on 0 to S3, on 1 to S1. What is the minimum number of states in an equivalent minimized Moore machine?
questions.explanationEn: S0 and S2 have identical output (0) and identical next states (S1, S3), so {S0, S2} are equivalent. S1 and S4 have identical output (1) and transition to {S0, S2}, so {S1, S4} are equivalent. S3 transitions to S3 on 0 (output 0) whereas S0 transitions to S1 (output 1), so S3 is distinct. Minimized count = 3 states.

questions.questionTextEn: How many 1s appear in the binary representation of the expression 3 × 2^9 + 5 × 2^5 + 7 × 2^1 + 1?
questions.explanationEn: 3 = 11_2 (2 ones at bits 10,9), 5 = 101_2 (2 ones at bits 7,5), 7 = 111_2 (3 ones at bits 3,2,1), and 1 = 1_2 (1 one at bit 0). None of the bit positions overlap (10,9,7,5,3,2,1,0), so total 1s = 2 + 2 + 3 + 1 = 8.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following circuits can be used to implement ANY 3-variable Boolean function F(A, B, C) without needing any additional logic gates (assuming true and complemented inputs are available)?
optionsEn: A 3-to-8 decoder alone (with no OR gate)
questions.explanationEn: An 8-to-1 MUX (tie inputs to 0/1), a 4-to-1 MUX (use C/C'/0/1 on data inputs), and an 8×1 ROM can each realize any 3-variable function without extra gates. A 3-to-8 decoder requires an external OR gate to sum minterms (C is false).

questions.questionTextEn: Let f(x, y, z) = (x ⊕ y) · (y ⊕ z). For how many input combinations (x, y, z) in {0, 1}^3 does f evaluate to 1?
questions.explanationEn: f = 1 requires x != y and y != z, which implies x = z != y. The only two 3-bit tuples satisfying this are (0, 1, 0) and (1, 0, 1), so the count is 2.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following representations correspond to the same signed decimal value -13 in an 8-bit system?
questions.explanationEn: +13 is 00001101. Sign-magnitude sets MSB=1: 10001101. 1's complement inverts all bits: 11110010. 2's complement adds 1: 11110011. Excess-128 stores -13 + 128 = 115 = 01110011. All four are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A 256 × 8 ROM is used as a combinational lookup table. How many input variables and how many independent Boolean functions of those variables can it simultaneously implement?
questions.explanationEn: 256 = 2^8 address locations correspond to 8 input variables, and an 8-bit word width provides 8 output lines, each realizing an arbitrary Boolean function of those 8 variables.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements regarding prime implicants (PIs) and essential prime implicants (EPIs) of a Boolean function are TRUE?
optionsEn: Every essential prime implicant must appear in every minimal SOP expression
A Boolean function can have zero essential prime implicants
Every minterm of a function is covered by at least one essential prime implicant
Removing a single literal from a prime implicant causes it to cover at least one 0-cell (maxterm) of the function
questions.explanationEn: EPIs are mandatory in every minimal SOP (A). Cyclic K-maps can have zero EPIs (B). By maximality, dropping any literal from a PI expands it to cover a 0 (D). Not every minterm needs an EPI (C is false).
